reviews.title: Misleading Pricing and Disappointing Business Model
reviews.text:
I am deeply disappointed with this app. It is advertised on the App Store as "Free with In-App Purchases," but that is completely misleading. In reality, there is no free tier or base version to use—you are given only a 3-day free trial before being forced into a paid subscription.
The expectation created by the app’s listing vs. the reality of what you get is totally mismatched. Branding an app as free when it is strictly a subscription-based service behind a brief trial feels intentionally deceptive and leads to a frustrating user experience right out of the gate. Be transparent with your pricing model.

reviews.title: Ai video is disappointing
reviews.text:
I downloaded Vids specifically because the advertising makes it look like you can upload a photo and turn it into a realistic AI video.
In practice, the Camera Motion feature mostly just moves or zooms the camera into a still image. I uploaded an image showing a driver on a road and wanted the vehicle to move naturally forward along the street. Instead, the generated video simply moved toward a house, which made no physical sense.
The biggest problem is the credit system. That unsuccessful 5-second generation cost me 98 AI credits, while the Pro plan only includes 230 credits per week. That means you can lose almost half of your weekly credits on one generation that doesn’t follow the intended movement.
For simple zoom or motion effects this may be useful, but based on my experience, the advertising creates much higher expectations for the AI image-to-video capability than the actual result delivers.

reviews.title: Not Ready to Compete with CapCut
reviews.text:
I purchased the Premium version expecting an AI-powered editor that could actually save me time. Instead, it wasted it.

The biggest disappointment? The AI couldn’t even generate a simple product video for my e-commerce store. It repeatedly errored out on a single-item project, making the feature completely unusable.

I then tried using the manual editing tools to create a Reel, hoping that experience would be better. It wasn’t. The editor feels clunky, unintuitive, and far behind competitors like CapCut. Simple editing tasks became frustrating, and the overall workflow slowed me down instead of speeding me up.

This app has potential, but right now it feels like a beta product being sold as a premium solution. Until the AI is reliable and the editor is significantly improved, I can’t recommend paying for it.

Save your money and stick with CapCut.

reviews.text: after using this for a few months, I caved in and spent almost $70 for the pro version. And after using it, in contrast with other software, both paid, and free, the amount of times that I had to go back and restart because it glitched out, didn’t save properly with the right effects that I spent so long to work on, and just general crashes, I am genuinely underwhelmed with what I’m getting. TikTok, the app that everybody uses, works better than this app. And it’s free. So if you want an app that actually works, just use CapCut or Final Cut, this app is pretty glitchy and is filled with bugs, and for the price, there’s so much better out there.
